html:
The United Nations Transitional Authority in Cambodia (UNTAC) ran parts of the country from 1992 to 1993, under the Paris Peace Agreements of 1991. It was the largest UN mission of its time.

It brought refugees home from Thai camps, tried to disarm the factions and organised an election in May 1993, in which about nine in ten voters took part despite threats. The royalist party won, but Hun Sen's party forced a power-sharing deal.

A new constitution restored the monarchy under Sihanouk. The Khmer Rouge boycotted the vote and fought on until 1998, when their movement collapsed after Pol Pot's death. See Vietnam's occupation.
sum: The United Nations Transitional Authority in Cambodia (UNTAC) ran parts of the country from 1992 to 1993, under the Paris Peace Agreements of 1991. It was the largest UN mission of its time.
